name: The Orange

scoring.report_note: Report team-level deltas only. Never rank teams — the orange measures the team's negotiation process, not talent.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for The Orange negotiation exercise. Scores at team level: how did interest exploration, information sharing and integrative thinking change across the negotiation?

instructions.pre: Before briefs are handed out. Each participant answers alone, about their own last week at work — not about the exercise.
instructions.post: Immediately after the debrief. Same items, now answered about the negotiation just completed, as a team.

items.pre_text: In disagreements, I ask what the other side needs it for.
items.post_text: During the negotiation, we asked (or regretted not asking) what they needed it for.

items.pre_text: I state my position early to anchor the discussion.
items.post_text: We opened with our position — and the anchor held all eight minutes.

items.pre_text: I share my real constraints when the other side hasn't earned it.
items.post_text: We held our brief back the whole time — even when sharing it would have paid.

items.pre_text: When two sides want the same thing, I look for what each actually needs.
items.post_text: Once the interests surfaced, a deal beyond 'half each' appeared quickly.

items.pre_text: Splitting the difference feels like the fair ending to me.
items.post_text: Half felt fair right up until the reveal showed what it cost.

items.pre_text: Before I counter an offer, I ask at least one question about it.
items.post_text: Before our next disagreement, we will ask one question before countering.

report.title: The Orange — team negotiation delta
sections: Agreement slips compared: splits, integrations, walks
One suggested question habit per team, derived from the largest positive delta
